notes.general: Check seasons: 2023, 2024 and 2025; test season: 2026, used once.

stages.prepare: Reads the prepared CSV into a pandas DataFrame and validates it.
stages.split: Split by calendar year, never at random. Expanding-window cross-validation: each of the three years before the latest is scored by a model trained only on earlier years, and the three mean absolute errors (MAE, the average miss in runs) are averaged. That average chooses the clues, settings and winning method, while the coefficients are fitted only on each fold's training years. The latest year is the test season, read once. Only IPL, BBL and full-member T20Is are scored.
stages.understand: Computes summary statistics to brief the AI agent before it proposes: each clue's correlation with the final total, runs added by wickets down, and mean totals by competition and year. They guide its proposals only; no model is fitted on them.
stages.frame: Regression on the final total, scored by MAE. Before any fitting, two references are scored on the check seasons: the TV projection and the average-total guess. The goal is to beat the TV projection by 3 runs of MAE on the test season.
stages.choose: Model selection. An idea (candidate model) is a set of clues (up to 8) plus three settings, set before fitting rather than learned: training window, recency weighting and training innings. The AI agent proposes ideas; code rejects any that are invalid, already tried, too small to train on or perfectly collinear, then fits and cross-validates the rest. The loop runs up to 6 rounds and stops after 2 without improvement. As the yardstick, the brute-force search tries all 24 combinations of settings, adding clues one at a time inside each. Whichever method's best idea has the lower cross-validated MAE wins, before the test season is read.
stages.fit: Fits the idea in closed form (least squares via the normal equations, not gradient descent): an intercept plus one coefficient per clue, weighted when recency weighting is on. A separate fit is made for each of the check seasons, on only the years before it, and the loop repeats this for every new idea. Solved directly in NumPy rather than scikit-learn (a test confirms identical coefficients) to stay within Vercel's size limit.
stages.assess: The winning idea and the other method's best are refitted on every year before the test season, then scored once on it alongside the TV projection and the average-total guess. Selection was already settled on cross-validated MAE, so this is an unbiased estimate of performance on a new season. Reports MAE, R², share within 10 and 20 runs, error as a % of a typical total, and bias, and whether the 3-run goal was met.
stages.interpret: Code works out a fixed set of named facts from the run and builds the blocks of the results section with template wording. A separate AI agent step then writes the titles and sentences, naming facts in braces and never writing a number: code rejects any reply with a digit, an unknown fact or text over the length limit, and fills every number in from the facts. If the model is absent or its reply is rejected, the template wording is used. A clue's importance is coefficient × interquartile range: how many runs a typical difference in that clue moves the prediction.

summary.text: Done once, before the agent runs, by scripts/prepare_data.py. The agent does not do any of this: it only ever sees the innings that were kept.
